method: Real documents, not PubChem grids: the pixel-exact method of build_ground_truth.py does not apply. Every structure was located by reading the PDF itself (pdftotext -layout, pdfimages, pdftoppm page crops). Each resolved molecule required TWO independent views to agree: a PubChem PUG-REST lookup (by a name or CAS number printed in the document, or - where the document prints no name - by a SMILES structure search on the drawn reading) AND a reading of the drawing itself. Every SMILES was round-tripped through RDKit Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.MolFromSmiles(s)) and its InChIKey recorded. Per-molecule `confidence` is one of: name_match (a name or CAS printed in the document resolves to the CID, and the drawing agrees), drawing_read (the document prints NO name; the structure was read off the drawing and then confirmed against a PubChem record by structure), or unresolved. `basis` states how each was pinned, including CID and page. `pixel_verified` is false everywhere - it is not achievable on real documents.
excluded: Structures that are DRAWN but carry no resolvable SMILES are held in each group's `unscoreable` array, NOT in `molecules`. That split is load-bearing: score_run.py calls Chem.MolFromSmiles(m['smiles']) on every entry of `molecules` and a null raises TypeError before its own error message, so a null-SMILES row there would crash the scorer. `unscoreable` holds Markush/R-group generics (generic: true) and structures with no second independent view (confidence: unresolved). Repeat drawings of one compound are collapsed to ONE row, because score_run.py matches predictions to molecules by NAME and counts recall per row - two rows for the same compound would let a single prediction score two recoveries.

molecules.note: Two views disagreed on the NAME: printed 'pyridine-2,4(1H,3H)-dione' vs a drawing with two ring nitrogens. The drawing wins, because 47 (a barbituric acid) and 6 (mavacamten, a pyrimidinedione) both require it.

unscoreable.name: 177Lu vipivotide tetraxetan
unscoreable.label: 5 (Pluvicto, 177Lu vipivotide tetraxetan)
unscoreable.note: Drawn in Figure 2 and as the Scheme 5 product as the 177Lu(III) CHELATE: a DOTA macrocycle with three carboxylates and 177Lu3+ drawn inside it, linked through a glycine to an aminomethyl-cyclohexyl-carbonyl, 2-naphthylalanine, lysine and a Glu-urea-Lys (PSMA-binding) motif. PubChem's 'vipivotide tetraxetan' CID 122706786 is the METAL-FREE ligand (C49H71N9O16) - it does not contain the lutetium the drawing shows. No PubChem record was found for the 177Lu complex, so the two views disagree and nothing is recorded; using the ligand CID would score a correct reading of the drawing as wrong.
